name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Thompson running with large money edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price 96% Republican
model.rationale: Thompson holds a heavily Republican-leaning district, has out-raised Bilger more than 13-to-1, and prediction markets give him roughly a 96% chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays safely Republican.
model.watch: A late, well-funded outside intervention or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the race, though nothing currently signals that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Thompson, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a north-central Pennsylvania district that leans about 19 points Republican. He has raised roughly $1.85 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democratic challenger Ray Bilger, who has raised about $140,000. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets price Thompson's chances at about 96 percent, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The Democratic environment nationally offers Bilger little help in a seat this red, and the forecast treats the race as safely Republican with high confidence.
